key_insight: The segmentation model was highly accurate for outlining vertebral arteries, but adding it to CTA did not improve and actually reduced reader diagnostic accuracy for vertebral artery dissection.
clinical_relevance: This suggests the tool may be useful for vessel visualization, but it is not yet ready to reliably support faster or better VAD diagnosis in routine acute care.
method: Trained a nnU-Net v2 vascular segmentation model on 101 CTA scans using five-fold cross-validation.
Externally tested the model on 40 CTA scans, including 22 VAD-positive and 18 VAD-negative cases.
Ran a 10-reader crossover study comparing CTA reads with vs without segmentation-based augmentation.
evidence_signal: The model achieved Dice similarity coefficient of 0.96 ± 0.01, but reader accuracy was significantly lower with augmentation than without (0.72 vs 0.84, P < 0.001).
watch_item: High segmentation performance did not translate into better diagnostic performance, so workflow integration and real-world validation remain important concerns.
paper_title: Does Deep Learning Vascular Segmentation on CTA Improve Vertebral Artery Dissection Detection?
